Goal: make packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js accept several files and stdin, as issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104 asks. Open one pull request that meets every line below.

Acceptance lines (each must hold at the PR head):
1. packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before
2. A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)
3. Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)
4. lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged
5. node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage
6. The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head

Steps:
1. Read packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js, packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js, packages/jsonl-lint/README.md and packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js. The current CLI reads only process.argv[2].
2. Do not edit packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js at all, so lint(text) stays byte-for-byte the same. All new behaviour goes in the bin file.
3. Rewrite packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js:
   - args = process.argv.slice(2). If there are none, write a usage line to stderr (keep the text `usage: jsonl-lint <file>` in it, for example `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`; the existing test matches /usage: jsonl-lint <file>/) and exit 2.
   - If `-` appears more than once, write a usage error to stderr and exit 2 before checking anything. Print nothing to stdout.
   - Go through the files in the order given. For `-`, read all of stdin (readFileSync(0, 'utf8') works) and use `-` as the name in output. For any other name, readFileSync(name, 'utf8'). If a read fails, write `jsonl-lint: cannot read <name>: <message>` to stderr, remember that a read failed, and go on to the next file. Do not stop.
   - For each file you can read, print `${name}:${line}: ${error with \r?\n replaced by a space}` to stdout for each problem from lint(text), the same as the single-file output now. Use the name exactly as given.
   - Exit code: 2 if any read failed, otherwise 1 if any file had a bad row, otherwise 0. A read failure gives 2 even when other files have bad rows. Their bad rows are still printed.
   - Keep it plain ESM with no dependencies.
4. Extend packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js with node:test cases. Run the CLI with spawnSync and pass stdin through the `input` option. Cover:
   - two clean files: exit 0, stdout empty
   - one bad file among several clean ones: exit 1, and stdout has only that file's `<file>:<line>: ` lines, in order
   - several bad files: their lines appear in argument order
   - `-` with clean stdin: exit 0
   - `-` with bad stdin: exit 1, and stdout starts with `-:<line>: `
   - a missing file among good ones, with one of the good ones bad: exit 2, stderr names the missing file, and the bad file's lines are still on stdout
   - two `-` arguments: exit 2, stderr not empty
   - no arguments: exit 2, usage on stderr
   Keep the existing tests passing.
5. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md: describe the usage `jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`, that `-` means stdin and is reported as `-`, that `-` may be given only once, the order of output, and the new exit codes. The exit codes are 0 when all files are clean, 1 when any row is bad, and 2 for no file, a second `-`, or any unreadable file. Say that when a file can't be read, the other files are still checked and reported.
6. Run `npm test` at the repository root and make sure it passes.
7. Commit, push and open one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test. Its body must contain the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. Wait for the `test` workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml) to finish on the PR head. If it fails, fix the cause and push again until it is green.
result.verifier:
Check the pull request for issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104 at its head commit. Run `npm ci` at the repository root first. In the commands below, B is packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js. Make a scratch dir with clean files c1.jsonl (`{"a":1}\n`) and c2.jsonl (`[1]\n\n"x"\n`), and a bad file b.jsonl (`{"a":1}\n{bad}\n{"t":`). Then run one check per expect line, in order.

Check 1. Expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before"
Run `node B c1.jsonl b.jsonl c2.jsonl`. Then copy b.jsonl to b2.jsonl and run `node B b.jsonl b2.jsonl`.
PASS: in the first run, stdout is exactly `b.jsonl:2: <msg>` and `b.jsonl:3: <msg>`, one per line, where each <msg> is the JSON.parse error for that row (compare with `node -e` printing lint() from packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js). In the second run, all of b.jsonl's lines come before all of b2.jsonl's lines, each with the file name exactly as given.
FAIL: a file is skipped, the order is wrong, the format differs, or a clean file prints anything.

Check 2. Expect: "A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)"
Run `printf '{bad}\n' | node B -`, `printf '{"a":1}\n' | node B -; echo $?`, and `printf '{}\n' | node B - c1.jsonl -; echo $?`.
PASS: the first run prints `-:1: <msg>` and exits 1. The second run prints nothing and exits 0. The third run exits 2 with a message on stderr.
FAIL: stdin is not read, the name is not `-`, or a second `-` does not exit 2.

Check 3. Expect: "Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)"
Run and record exit codes:
- `node B c1.jsonl c2.jsonl` should exit 0.
- `node B c1.jsonl b.jsonl` should exit 1.
- `node B` (no args) should exit 2, with stderr not empty.
- `node B c1.jsonl missing.jsonl b.jsonl` should exit 2. stderr must name missing.jsonl, and stdout must still contain the b.jsonl:2 and b.jsonl:3 lines.
PASS: all four hold.
FAIL: any one does not.

Check 4. Expect: "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged"
Run `git fetch origin main` and `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js`. Also run `node --test packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js`.
PASS: the lint function's body and signature have no diff, and the lint tests pass.
FAIL: the lint function is changed.

Check 5. Expect: "node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage"
Read packages/jsonl-lint/test/*.test.js and run `npm test --workspace packages/jsonl-lint`. Read packages/jsonl-lint/README.md.
PASS: the tests pass, and they include node:test cases for each of: two clean files, one bad file among several, `-` with clean stdin, `-` with bad stdin, a missing file among good ones, two `-` arguments, and no arguments. The README documents multiple file arguments and `-` for stdin.
FAIL: any of those cases is missing, a test fails, or the README does not document this usage.

Check 6. Expect: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head"
Run `gh pr view <pr> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --json body,headRefOid,state` and `gh pr checks <pr> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test`. Run `npm test` at the repository root at the head.
PASS: there is one open PR on that repo, and its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. The `test` workflow check for the head commit succeeded, and the local `npm test` exits 0.
FAIL: the closing line is missing, the workflow check is failing or missing at the head, or npm test fails.

Advisory (not pass/fail): note whether a second `-` exits before printing any lint output, and whether an unreadable `-` or a directory argument is handled gracefully.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #104 and the harness accepted them. I made no code changes, commits or PRs.

**Builder brief:**
- **Scope:** all the new behaviour goes in `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js`. `packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` is not touched, so `lint(text)` stays the same.
- **The CLI:**
  - It checks each file in the order given and prints bad rows in the same `<file>:<line>: <error>` format as now.
  - `-` reads from stdin and is reported as `-`.
  - A second `-` is a usage error: exit 2 before anything is checked.
  - A file that can't be read gets an error on stderr, and the other files are still checked.
- **Exit codes:** 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read, otherwise 1 if any row is bad, otherwise 0. I decided that an unreadable file gives 2 even when other files have bad rows, because the issue's wording reads that way.
- **Tests and README:** the new `node:test` cases cover every case the issue lists, the README documents the usage, and the usage message keeps `usage: jsonl-lint <file>` so the existing test still passes.
- **The PR:** one PR whose body has the `Closes …/issues/104` line. The builder waits for the `test` workflow and fixes it until it is green.

**Verifier brief:** six checks, one per expect line, in order. Each one runs commands at the PR head:
1. Several files, including a clean, bad, clean mix: every bad row is printed in order and in the right format.
2. `-` with clean and bad stdin, and two `-` arguments exiting 2.
3. The exit code for each case: all clean, one bad, no arguments, and a missing file among others whose bad rows must still print.
4. A `git diff` of `src/index.js` against `origin/main`, plus the existing lint tests.
5. The tests cover each listed case and pass, and the README documents the usage.
6. `gh pr view` and `gh pr checks` for the closing line and a green workflow, plus `npm test` run locally.

Two extra points are under an Advisory heading and don't affect pass or fail: whether a second `-` stops before printing any output, and whether a directory argument is handled cleanly.
